notes.bambi: Sympathy, not apology: said when someone is ill, tired or has had bad luck. Reply: Asante, or Nimeshapoa.
notes.samahani: An apology, or to get someone’s attention.
notes.hasira: Ana hasira: he or she is angry.

guidebook.intro: Some feelings are things you have (nina furaha, “I have happiness”), others are things that have happened to you (nimechoka, “I have got tired”).

tips.title: Having a feeling
body: Many feelings are nouns you **have**: **nina furaha** (I’m happy, “I have joy”), **nina huzuni** (I’m sad), **nina wasiwasi** (I’m worried), **ana hasira** (she’s angry).
Others are **-me-** verbs, for a state you have got into: **nimefurahi** (I’m glad), **nimekasirika** (I’m angry), **nimechoka** (I’m tired), **nimeshangaa** (I’m surprised).

tips.title: Short forms: na-
body: In everyday speech, **nina-** often shrinks to **na-**: **ninaogopa** becomes **naogopa** (I’m afraid), **ninakupenda** becomes **nakupenda** (I love you). You already know **nataka**.

culture.title: Pole and hongera
body: **Pole** is said for any misfortune, from a stubbed toe to a death in the family, and **hongera** for any good news: a new baby, a new job, a passed exam. Both are said often and warmly.
